title: Queen Lokamahadevi commissioned Pattadakal's Virupaksha Temple
body: The Virupaksha Temple at Pattadakal in Karnataka dates to about 740 CE. Queen Lokamahadevi had it built to commemorate a victory of her husband, a ruler of the Chalukya dynasty.
takeaway: A temple can record a royal commission and how its patron wanted a victory remembered.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Group of Monuments at Pattadakal (1987)

title: Peru's Caral had six large pyramidal structures 5,000 years ago
body: Caral was built on a dry terrace overlooking Peru's Supe valley. The site of roughly 626 hectares contains large stone and earth platforms and sunken circular courts.
takeaway: Monumental public spaces give archaeologists clues to how an early city gathered its people.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Sacred City of Caral-Supe (2009)
